text: When you design a REST API, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and simple endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so that developers can easily understand what each one does. Second, always return the correct status codes. For example, use 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, keep your documentation up to date, because good examples help people use your API faster. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. These simple rules make your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
